prompt: A friend who's been building a Postgres rewrite with coding agents keeps telling me we should be more ambitious with the software we build. I half agree, but most AI-built projects I see are junk. Write a blog post taking his line seriously: what has actually changed about what one programmer can build now, drawing on your own experiments, and why people aren't taking advantage of it.

I keep seeing devs who just have the LLM write code and paste errors back to it until it works, without really thinking. Models are getting good enough that maybe that's fine? Is there any future where that approach actually pays off for them?

Write an essay on why some people seem to see software bugs everywhere while most people, including the teams that ship the software, don't notice them at all. Draw on your own experience, and say why it matters for programmers in particular.
honest question: why do I seem to run into way more bugs than everyone around me? am I just using computers weird?
Do you think a lot of what we call being 'good with computers' is really just knowing how to dodge bugs?
